title: Delay gave no clear added 50 Hz plasticity prediction value in four selected Allen slice groups
abstract: We tested whether transmission delay helps predict 50 Hz response changes beyond cell labels, soma distance and voltage strength. Allen Synaptic Physiology r2.1 supplied 1,687 selected connections in mouse visual cortex and human temporal cortex. We held out whole inferred donors in five folds with five splits. Adding log delay increased mean squared prediction error in all four species and response-sign groups. No primary group or planned sensitivity check showed a clear positive gain. The primary human excitatory interval indicated worse prediction, but donor weighting weakened that result. These findings limit one additive ridge predictor. They do not establish biological independence. Slice selection, shared fit error, inferred donors, region and species differences, and a small human inhibitory sample limit transfer. Original code, aggregate evidence, a figure, source hashes and external retrieval instructions support reproduction. External records and derived record-level tables are not bundled.

display.caption: Added delay prediction value in four selected groups. Points show reference MSE minus delay-model MSE. Bars show conditional donor-bootstrap 98.75 percent intervals. Positive values favor delay.

citations.reason: Prior distance test informs donor grouping and distance limit. No code or record-level evidence is reused.
